_comment: SPECCED, NOT BUILT. Three sparsity / multi-scale workloads, held until the tolerance-driven refinement (py_octree_tol) has been measured on the three space-filling ones: testing the sparse regime with no accuracy knob would repeat the confound F1 names (README, Performance). Each validates as a workload and would run unchanged once `held` is removed. They never produce a record while held; SELECTION.md counts them at the top.

conditions.why: one point charge in a 40-unit box: 99.9% of the volume is more than 10 source-radii away; the regime the octree's author_claim names

held.reason: the sparse regime is where placement is supposed to pay; measuring it with py_octree, whose error cannot move, would again confound placement with the missing accuracy knob
held.settles: at matched accuracy, does the tolerance-driven octree need fewer points than the uniform grid, and by how much, when most of the box is empty (F2's 'unmeasured' cell)
held.build_after: py_octree_tol matched-accuracy rows on dipole / quadrupole / wire_charge are in results.jsonl

conditions.why: a 12 x 12 sheet of 144 charges on one face of the box and nothing else: the field is a thin layer near z = -2 and smooth elsewhere; two length scales, sheet pitch 0.33 and box 4

sources._sheet: 12x12 pitch 0.3333 on z=-2; the runner expands this record into 144 sources when the workload is un-held

held.reason: thin-layer fields are the second regime adaptivity is claimed for; the same confound applies until a knob exists, and the sheet expansion (144 sources) is not written
held.settles: whether the tolerance-driven octree concentrates leaves in the layer and holds the far-field error at the same tolerance with fewer points than a uniform grid whose pitch must resolve the layer everywhere
held.build_after: py_octree_tol measured on the three space-filling workloads; then write the sheet expansion in the runner

conditions.why: a dipole of separation 0.02 at the origin and a single charge 1.5 units away: features at 0.02 and at 1.5, a 75:1 scale ratio in one box

held.reason: the multi-scale regime; a uniform grid must be pitched at the small scale everywhere, an adaptive one only near it, but only if its refinement reads the field, which py_octree's does not
held.settles: the point-count ratio at matched accuracy as the scale ratio grows; with the uniform grid at 75:1 this is res >= 200 per axis, 8e6 points, which is the memory-ceiling cell as well
held.build_after: py_octree_tol measured on the three space-filling workloads
